title: His Friends Think He Is the Rich One. Overdrawn Twice This Year.
blurb: A friend at dinner says Dev must be saving loads.

title: Their Credit Card Is at Zero for Eight Weeks a Year
blurb: Sam and Jo's credit card hits zero on the third of April and stays there for eight weeks.

title: Two Cliffs, Six Months Apart
blurb: March: the fixed rate ends and the payment rises by about £260.

title: Their Christmas Money Arrives in January
blurb: Marcus's fourth-quarter commission is paid in January.

title: Same £2,600. One Has a £650 Envelope.
blurb: Two women on the same grade, same £2,600, and last year both had a dentist and a laptop go wrong.

title: They Saw the University Bill Coming for a Year. It Still Went on the Card.
blurb: Everyone in the Okafor house knew the date their eldest starts university.

title: Their Second-Biggest Bill Has Never Been Discussed
blurb: Nursery is the bill Tom and Aisha talk about: £1,120 a month.

title: Line 14 on Her Statement: £9.99, Forever
blurb: A budgeting app, £9.99 a month, on Anita's statement for six years.

title: £400 a Month, and He Found Out From the Statement
blurb: Grace has sent her mother £400 a month for six years, as a transfer with no name.

title: The Second Car Is £510 a Month, Not £18,000
blurb: The lease on the second car ends in March, and unless something changes they will sign another in a showroom in twenty minutes.

title: Christmas Costs Them Three Months. It Still Surprises Them.
blurb: After rent, bills, food and the car, Sam and Jo have £300 a month spare.

title: £4,000 Lands Four Times a Year. Where Does It Go?
blurb: Part of Dev's pay arrives as a lump every quarter.

title: They Earn £7,200 a Month. The Joint Account Ends on £81.
blurb: Tom and Aisha each put £2,200 into the joint account three years ago, when it was fair.

title: Day 30 of Her First Budget: 52 / 41 / 6
blurb: Day thirty of Leah's first budget and she was about to quit: the template said 50 / 30 / 20 and her month said 52 / 41 / 6, with wants £286 over on nothing wild.

title: £14,000 Saved. A Year, She Thought.
blurb: Anita has £14,000 saved and calls it a year of runway.

title: £616 a Month. They Would Say They Have No Debt.
blurb: Ask Marcus and Jen if they have any debt and they will say no.

title: Same Pay. One Knows Where It Went.
blurb: Two nurses, same ward, same band, same shifts.

title: £2,000 of the Bonus Went Somewhere. Nobody Can Say Where.
blurb: £2,000 of Femi's £11,000 bonus went somewhere in the spring and neither he nor Grace can say where.

title: £2,000 a Month in Pay Rises. He Kept £70.
blurb: Dev's take-home has gone up £2,000 a month in four years and his savings have gone up £70.

title: Paid in Full. Still a Month Behind.
blurb: Priya pays her credit card in full every month and is a month behind.

title: Their Budget Is Wrong Every Month of the Year
blurb: Marcus and Jen's budget is wrong every month of the year, and not because they overspend.

title: £80 More a Month Bought Her Three Days
blurb: Priya gave her eating-out budget £80 more a month and the money ran out three days later than before: the 23rd instead of the 20th.

title: £14.99 a Month for an App She Never Opened
blurb: On Leah's bank statement: a fitness app she has never opened, taking £14.99 a month since January.

title: Six Years of Tax Bills From Savings, Each One a Surprise
blurb: For six years Anita has paid her tax out of savings, twice a year, and been surprised both times: £66,600 in all.

title: How Much Emergency Fund? Every Answer Is Wrong (UK)
blurb: Six months of expenses is the standard emergency fund advice. On £150 a month spare that is 45 months — and only if nothing goes wrong in the meantime.
